verdict_summary: A 26-domain sweep can only find rules that are missing from a domain it was told exists, and it can only ever find them by proving a grep returns nothing. That shape has three consequences. First, it is additive by construction: 264 findings, and not one of them says an existing rule is wrong, too expensive, or should be deleted. For an estate whose owner's actual complaint is that rules get forgotten or outranked, a method that can only grow the law layer is pointed the wrong way. Second, nothing lives in the seams: no agent owned the conflict between an owner taste decision and a WCAG requirement, between the imagery floor and the LCP budget, or between what the ToS promises a customer and what it promises a salon, so each of those was found only as an instance inside one domain and never as the arbitration rule that is actually missing. Third, every agent audited the state the estate is in, and the estate has never been in the state that matters: pre-launch is treated as a permanent condition (there is a gate enforcing the pre-launch framing and no artifact anywhere naming what ends it), so the whole sweep is an audit of a rehearsal. The three largest things the sweep did not see are structural, not domain-shaped: there is exactly one Supabase project and the local .env.local carries its service-role key, so dev, seed scripts, kill-tests and production are the same live database; the precedence chain that resolves every conflict in this estate has no legal or safety tier at all; and a salon can be activated into the marketplace by an enforced code gate but has no defined way to leave it. My recommendation on the 264 stands separately from my own list: adopt the small verified-and-cheap subset now, and treat the rest as a backlog that must shrink before launch, not a list to be written into doctrine this month.

structural_blind_spots.blind_spot: Cross-domain arbitration. No agent could propose the rule that resolves a conflict between two domains' floors, because such a rule belongs to neither domain.
structural_blind_spots.why_missed: Each agent was scoped inside one named domain and asked what was missing from it. A conflict between the design imagery floor and the performance LCP budget appeared only as hierarchy-density-09, filed as a design gap. The WCAG-versus-owner-taste conflict appeared only as accessibility-01, filed as an a11y gap. In both cases the actual missing artifact is an arbitration rule that no domain owns.

structural_blind_spots.blind_spot: The estate's relationship to time. Nobody audited the rule set against a state the product has never occupied.
structural_blind_spots.why_missed: Agents compare current code to current law. Both are pre-launch. The rules that become wrong on the day of the first real booking (the prelaunch-reality-gate's whole discriminator, the no-real-customers memory entry, the pre-launch framing that makes every severity a conditional) are correct today, so no absence-proving grep can flag them.

structural_blind_spots.blind_spot: The business as an artifact. What Solen promises each side, what it refuses to promise, and who wins when the two sides conflict.
structural_blind_spots.why_missed: The domain list was technical and craft-shaped. The Terms of Service were read by exactly one agent, and only as a source of prose-versus-code mismatches (trust-01 to trust-06). Nobody was asked whether the promises themselves are the right ones, coherent with each other, or keepable by one person.

structural_blind_spots.blind_spot: The owner as a component of the system: capacity, concurrent work, availability, and what happens when they are unreachable.
structural_blind_spots.why_missed: No domain was called 'the human'. law-system-meta came closest with no-second-operator-onboarding-bound, but scoped it to a fresh agent's read time, not to the owner's own throughput. So 27 simultaneously ACTIVE workstreams and a scattered, undated owner-blocked backlog are invisible: they are not code and not law, they are load.

structural_blind_spots.blind_spot: Endings and exits as lifecycle stages, rather than as defects inside an existing flow.
structural_blind_spots.why_missed: An absence-proving agent finds a missing check inside a flow that exists. A flow that was never built at all produces no anchor to grep against. Salon offboarding has no route, no doc and no mention, so there was nothing for any domain agent to find missing from it.

structural_blind_spots.blind_spot: Outcome measurement. Whether any of this made the product work.
structural_blind_spots.why_missed: Every domain measures conformance of its own artifact: pixels against floors, routes against contracts, tokens against a palette. Nobody's domain was 'did a customer book'. The estate consequently has an extremely precise measurement culture pointed entirely at inputs.

structural_blind_spots.blind_spot: Environment topology. Which database is production, which credentials exist where, and what a dev process may touch.
structural_blind_spots.why_missed: This sits above application code and below infrastructure. Agents read app/, lib/, supabase/migrations/ and the law docs. The fact that .env.local is a symlink pointing every worktree at the production project ref, with the service-role key, is in none of those places.

structural_blind_spots.blind_spot: Anything the estate itself has never named. The 26-domain taxonomy was derived from the estate being audited, so it inherits that estate's existing blind spots exactly.
structural_blind_spots.why_missed: A sweep organised by the subject's own categories cannot discover a category the subject lacks. Design got seven domains; the business got one; the owner's own sustainability got a fraction of one; the customer's actual outcomes got none.

structural_blind_spots.blind_spot: The wrongness of existing rules. The method can prove a rule is absent, never that a present rule is harmful, overpriced, or should be deleted.
structural_blind_spots.why_missed: Each agent's evidence standard was a grep proving absence. There is no symmetric procedure for proving a rule costs more than it prevents, so the sweep's output is monotonically additive against an estate whose stated pain is rule volume and rules being outranked.

net_new_principles.title: There is no staging: dev, seed scripts, kill-tests and production are one live database
net_new_principles.principle: Name exactly one Supabase project as PRODUCTION and write its ref in a single place. No local dev process, seed script, kill-test, migration trial or agent session may hold that project's service-role key. Until a second project exists, every script that can write (seed, backfill, cleanup, kill-test, apply_migration) must read the configured project ref, compare it to the production ref, and refuse to run on a match unless the owner passes an explicit, per-invocation confirmation. Provisioning a second project is the real fix; the refusal check is what holds the line until then.
net_new_principles.why: The whole estate's safety story assumes a boundary that does not exist. The local .env.local is a symlink shared by every worktree, it carries SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, and the only Supabase URL present in any env file is the same project ref the orchestrator queried live. Claude Code runs with defaultMode bypassPermissions. So a single wrong script in a dev session writes to the same 150-table database that will hold real bookings and real money, with RLS bypassed by the service role, and no dialog in the way. Every backend finding in this run assumes an attacker or a bug; this is the case where a routine local command is sufficient. It is also why the migration-replay landmines the orchestrator found (the amenity-fabrication migration, the reviews RLS policy) are more dangerous than they look: the only database a replay could ever land on is the live one.
net_new_principles.where_it_should_live: A new ENVIRONMENTS row in the project CLAUDE.md design/ops contract, plus _rules/DB_SCHEMA.md section 1, plus _plans/OPS_RUNBOOK.md
net_new_principles.enforcement: A production-ref-guard PreToolUse hook that denies any Bash command containing the production project ref or invoking a known write-script while no confirmation flag is fresh, and a runtime assert at the top of every script in scripts/ that touches Supabase. Both are cheap and testable against a fake ref before arming.
net_new_principles.local_evidence: /Users/sulo/Documents/solen/.claude/worktrees/quirky-ellis-ef5559/.env.local is a symlink to /Users/sulo/Documents/solen/.env.local; it contains one SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE key and NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=https://tocfnsmxmdxkrcmjzzdw.supabase.co, which is the same ref the orchestrator ran its live SELECTs against. grep across all .env* files returns exactly one supabase.co host. /Users/sulo/.claude/settings.json line 4 sets defaultMode to bypassPermissions.

net_new_principles.title: The precedence chain has no legal or safety tier, so a taste rejection silently outranks a statutory floor
net_new_principles.principle: Insert one tier into the precedence chain, directly below the owner's live literal ask and above everything else: statutory and safety floors. Named members: WCAG 2.1 A and AA on published surfaces, Swiss nFADP and GDPR obligations, the Preisbekanntgabeverordnung price-display rules, and any representation already made in the shipped Terms of Service. When a taste decision, a LOCKFILE row or a gate would breach one of these, it is not applied and it is not silently resolved either way: the session stops, names the specific requirement, and offers the owner an option that satisfies both. The owner may still overrule, but the overrule is recorded as a knowing legal exception with a date, not as a design preference.
net_new_principles.why: The chain in the project CLAUDE.md runs owner ask, gates, LOCKFILE, pinned blocks, TASTE_LOG, memory, global rules, checklists. The word legal appears in it only as a UI-copy exemption. The consequence has already happened and this sweep found it three separate times without naming the cause: focus outlines are removed unconditionally for every device because rings were rejected on taste three times (accessibility-01), pinch-zoom is disabled sitewide (accessibility-03, typography-01), and a grey authorized for informational text computes at 2.54:1 (accessibility-05). Each was filed as an accessibility gap. The actual defect is upstream: an aesthetic preference and a legal floor were fed into a chain that has no way to tell them apart, and aesthetics sat higher. Adding twenty a11y rules does not fix a chain that will outrank them again next time.
net_new_principles.where_it_should_live: The Precedence chain block in the project CLAUDE.md, mirrored in the header of _design-system/TASTE_LOG.md and in ~/.claude/LAW_SYSTEM.md section on conflict resolution
net_new_principles.enforcement: Behavioural at the chain level, plus a legal-conflict branch in the existing rejection-escalation hook: when an owner rejection matches a term on a short list (focus, zoom, contrast, consent, price display, cancellation terms), the hook injects the specific requirement and requires the both-satisfying alternative to be offered before the rejection is applied.
net_new_principles.local_evidence: grep -niE '\blegal\b' on /Users/sulo/.claude/CLAUDE.md and /Users/sulo/.claude/LAW_SYSTEM.md returns zero hits; in the project CLAUDE.md the only hits are the imagery-floor exemption list and 'omission is legal only for null data'. The chain itself is the 8-item Precedence block in the project CLAUDE.md. Digest instances: accessibility-01, accessibility-03, accessibility-05, typography-01, ethics-psychology-01, ethics-psychology-04, copy-i18n-11.

net_new_principles.title: Nothing in the estate defines the end of pre-launch, or lists what becomes wrong on that day
net_new_principles.principle: Maintain one LAUNCH.md with two sections and nothing else. Section A: the binary conditions that must all be true before the first real customer booking is accepted, each either true or false, no partial credit. Section B: the flip list, every gate file, memory entry, doctrine sentence and product default that becomes wrong the moment we are live, each with its exact path and its post-launch value. Launch is executed by walking section B, not by an announcement. Until section A is complete, any claim that a fix can wait because we are pre-launch must name the section A item it is parked behind.
net_new_principles.why: Pre-launch is currently a permanent, self-reinforcing frame with no exit. A Stop gate enforces the conditional framing of every bug (prelaunch-reality-gate.py: a pre-launch bug is a WOULD, never a DID), a memory entry restates it, and the only way out is a manual skip flag. That gate is right about the past failure it was built for, and it also means the cheapest correct answer to any severity question is 'we are not live yet', forever, with no counter and no deadline. The sharpest evidence that the estate knows how to do this properly is that it already does it for the other side of the marketplace: POST /api/salon/go-live refuses to activate a salon without Stripe onboarding complete, a cover photo, at least one active service and prior admin approval. A salon has an enforced readiness gate. The platform has none.
net_new_principles.where_it_should_live: A new _plans/LAUNCH.md, referenced from the project CLAUDE.md pinned blocks and from _plans/ACTIVE.md as workstream row zero
net_new_principles.enforcement: prelaunch-reality-gate.py reads a LAUNCH_STATE value from LAUNCH.md instead of assuming pre-launch, so the day the state flips the gate inverts on its own. system-health-check.py gains one invariant: LAUNCH.md exists, every path named in section B resolves, and no section A item is undated.
net_new_principles.local_evidence: /Users/sulo/.claude/hooks/prelaunch-reality-gate.py, docstring: 'State impact in the conditional until the owner says we are live', escape hatch is a manual flag file. Memory entry project_prelaunch_no_real_customers.md. app/api/salon/go-live/route.ts lines 41-86 implement the salon-side readiness gate (approved_at, isStripeReady, cover_photo_url, serviceCount >= 1). No equivalent file exists for the platform: no go-live, launch-readiness or day-one document in _plans/ (111 files checked).

net_new_principles.title: A salon can be activated into the marketplace and has no defined way to leave it
net_new_principles.principle: Every entry into the marketplace has a symmetric, defined exit. Before any further onboarding work, write the salon exit spec and answer, in order: what happens to already-confirmed future bookings, to money in flight and to the next payout, to the salon's reviews and its public URL, to the client records the salon authored, and how long each of those lives after departure. Build the route or write the manual procedure the admin follows, but the exit may not remain undefined. The same applies to a customer who leaves with a booking in the future.
net_new_principles.why: POST /api/salon/go-live sets is_active true through an enforced checklist. There is no owner-initiated deactivation, offboarding or go-dark path anywhere in app/api: every is_active false write in the codebase belongs to something else (a retail item, a dynamic-pricing rule, a recurring booking, an off-peak rule, a discovery item, or the admin reject route). Account deletion is not an exit either: both /api/profile/delete and /api/profile/request-deletion refuse while the owner's salon has confirmed or pending bookings, which is correct in itself and leaves the salon with exactly two ways out, be rejected by an admin, or personally cancel every future booking and then delete the account. A salon that wants to leave in week three will therefore either abandon its listing while still bookable, which is the worst possible outcome for a customer, or generate a manual support incident that has no written procedure. This is not a defect inside a flow, which is why no domain agent could find it: the flow does not exist.
net_new_principles.where_it_should_live: A new lifecycle section in _docs/BACKEND.md, the Terms of Service section on account termination, and _plans/OPS_RUNBOOK.md for the manual admin steps
net_new_principles.enforcement: Written procedure first, since a manual runbook is the honest answer at 28 salons. One test asserts that a deactivated salon's future bookings are visible in an admin queue and that the salon's public URL returns something coherent rather than a 404 with live bookings behind it.
net_new_principles.local_evidence: app/api/salon/go-live/route.ts POST sets is_active true. grep for is_active false writes across app and lib returns only retail/route.ts:131, dynamic-pricing/route.ts:86, bookings/recurring/[id]/route.ts:32, off-peak/route.ts:206, admin/discovery routes, admin/salons/[id]/reject/route.ts:38 and salons/route.ts:708 (pending approval). app/api/profile/delete/route.ts:18-34 and request-deletion/route.ts:60-80 both block deletion while the owner's salon has confirmed or pending bookings.

net_new_principles.title: Every customer-facing feature ships with one number that says whether it worked
net_new_principles.principle: A customer-facing feature is not shippable until its workstream row names one observable number that tells you whether it did its job, where that number is read from, and the date it will be looked at. If no such number exists, the row says 'unmeasurable, shipping on taste' in those words. Once live, that number is checked on its date and the result is written next to the claim, whether it confirms or refutes it.
net_new_principles.why: This estate measures its inputs to three significant figures and its outputs not at all. It has a geometry checker, an emphasis budget with a 30 percent weight ceiling, an anchor ratio floor of 1.8x, a type-size budget and a 33 percent imagery floor, all measured on rendered pixels. Searching _design-system, _plans and _docs for a north star, an activation rate or any success-metric target returns three incidental files, and PostHog error capture was never even switched on (observability-5). The consequence is not just that nobody knows if the design law works. It is that the design law cannot be wrong: with no outcome number, a floor can only ever be complied with or violated, never disproved, which is exactly how an estate accumulates 410,000 words of unfalsifiable craft law. One number per feature is also the only cheap defence against that, and it costs a cell in a table.
net_new_principles.where_it_should_live: A new 'measure' column in the _plans/ACTIVE.md workstream index, and one line in _design-system/SENIOR_SCORECARD.md as a sixth dimension
net_new_principles.enforcement: The existing workstreams-index-guard hook gains one check: a row whose status is ACTIVE and whose type is customer-facing may not have an empty measure cell. Pre-launch the cell may legitimately say 'after launch, date TBD by LAUNCH.md'.
net_new_principles.local_evidence: grep for north.?star, activation rate, conversion target, success metric or KPI target across _design-system/, _plans/ and _docs/ returns only RESTRAINT_TEST.md, research/PSYCH_BUSINESS_IMPACT.md and DASHBOARD_OVERHAUL.md, none of which sets a Solen target. Contrast: the project CLAUDE.md FLOORS LAW and EMPHASIS BUDGET blocks specify at least nine numeric input thresholds.

net_new_principles.title: No law in this estate has ever been checked against a real salon owner or a real customer, and the docs do not say so
net_new_principles.principle: Every law that claims a user outcome, that users scan a certain way, that a treatment converts, that a screen reads busy, carries a source tier in its own row: measured-on-Solen, external-evidence, or owner-taste. Owner-taste is a legitimate and final answer and simply may not be written or reported as though it were user evidence. From the first month after launch, at least one outcome-claiming law per quarter is checked against real behaviour or one real salon-owner conversation, and the check's result is written into the row, including when it refutes the law.
net_new_principles.why: Every design law here descends from three sources: the owner's eye, captures of other companies' products, and literature. The 28 salons are seeds and there are no customers, so no rule in the estate has ever met a user. That is fine and normal pre-launch. What is not fine is that the writing does not distinguish the tiers, so an owner preference and a sourced finding read identically in the same document, and the estate's own rule 15 discipline of tiering claims was applied to external statistics and never turned on its own craft law. The specific risk this creates is the one the sweep already stumbled on: the imagery floor was specified at 33 percent against seeded content, and the live browse page renders 0 percent, because the floor was never validated against what real salons actually upload.
net_new_principles.where_it_should_live: A source-tier field in the block header format of _design-system/RATIONALE.md and _design-system/PSYCHOLOGY.md, and one line in the precedence block explaining that owner-taste tier is final but not evidence
net_new_principles.enforcement: Extend the existing stat-source-gate.py from external persuasion statistics to internal outcome claims: a sentence asserting user behaviour inside a design doc needs a tier marker or it does not get written.
net_new_principles.local_evidence: grep for user interview, usability test or customer interview across _design-system/ and _plans/ returns only three research files that cite external literature (PSYCH_PSYCHOLOGY.md, PSYCH_CONVERSION.md, TASTE_GROUPING.md), none reporting a Solen user. The orchestrator's live measurement records /de/basel at 0 percent imagery against a 33 percent floor, with salon_photos holding 0 rows for 28 salons.

net_new_principles.title: One-way doors and two-way doors get the same ceremony, so the cheap decisions are over-locked and the irreversible ones went in unremarked
net_new_principles.principle: Classify a decision before locking it. A one-way door is anything a customer, a salon, a payment processor or a search engine can come to rely on: a money representation, a schema shape, a public URL, a Terms of Service sentence, a payout policy. It requires a written rationale, a stated migration story for changing it later, and an explicit owner sign-off. A two-way door is anything reversible in an afternoon: a shadow value, a radius, a copy string, an animation curve. It gets decided fast, marked cheap-to-reverse, and is never allowed to consume a locking ceremony. Every LOCKFILE row and TASTE_LOG entry states which kind it is.
net_new_principles.why: The estate applies maximum ceremony uniformly, and the result is inverted. Reversible aesthetics are frozen with dated owner stamps and defended by gates, while genuine one-way doors slipped in with no ceremony at all: two money representations coexist in the live schema with no law choosing one (integer Rappen in the booking path, numeric(10,2) in the retail-era tables), no law governs what happens when a salon's public slug would change (ia-navigation-06), and the shipped Terms of Service made at least three enforceable promises with no code behind them (trust-01, trust-02, trust-03). The cost of over-locking a two-way door is velocity. The cost of under-locking a one-way door is a migration you cannot perform because customers are standing on it.
net_new_principles.where_it_should_live: A door column in _design-system/LOCKFILE.md rows and the _design-system/TASTE_LOG.md entry template, plus one paragraph in ~/.claude/LAW_SYSTEM.md on decision classes
net_new_principles.enforcement: Authoring-time: the taste-log entry template requires the field. Additionally, a short one-way-door register listing the handful that exist (money unit, slug scheme, ToS clauses, payout timing, booking reference format) so a session can check membership in one read instead of inferring it.
net_new_principles.local_evidence: Orchestrator live verification section 3: bookings.paid_amount, platform_fee and net_amount are integer Rappen while retail-era migrations carry net_amount numeric(10,2), with no law choosing. Digest: ia-navigation-06 (no slug-change law), trust-01/02/03 (ToS promises with no implementation). Contrast the ceremony given to reversible values in the project CLAUDE.md design contract table.

net_new_principles.title: Twenty-seven workstreams are marked ACTIVE for one person, and the index cannot even distinguish them by number
net_new_principles.principle: Cap concurrently ACTIVE workstreams at three. Starting a fourth requires pausing a named one in the same edit. Every other row is PAUSED, QUEUED or DONE. Workstream ids are unique and never reused. An index whose ACTIVE marker is true of twenty-seven rows is not a status, it is noise, and the index exists specifically so that a compaction or a fresh session can restore state in one read.
net_new_principles.why: _plans/ACTIVE.md currently shows 27 rows marked ACTIVE, 9 PAUSED, 2 BLOCKED and 21 DONE, with at least twelve id collisions (two rows each numbered 8, 16, 17, 18, 19, 26, 29, 30, 31, 32, 33 and 34), against 111 files in _plans/. The file's own header explains it exists because the previous single-file model lost a workstream entirely. The failure mode has simply changed shape: nothing is lost now, everything is merely equally active, which produces the same outcome for a session trying to work out what matters. This is also the mechanism behind the branch graveyard the orchestrator measured, 1,686 commits on 40 unmerged branches: work is started faster than it is closed, and no artifact bounds the rate.
net_new_principles.where_it_should_live: The header rules of _plans/ACTIVE.md, and the topic-switch rule already written at the bottom of that file
net_new_principles.enforcement: The existing workstreams-index-guard hook already blocks writes that drop the index marker. Extend it with two assertions that are pure counting: at most three ACTIVE rows, and no duplicate id. Both fail loudly on the current file, which is the point.
net_new_principles.local_evidence: /Users/sulo/Documents/solen/.claude/worktrees/quirky-ellis-ef5559/_plans/ACTIVE.md, status counts measured this session: 27 ACTIVE, 21 DONE, 9 PAUSED, 2 BLOCKED. Duplicate ids visible in the rendered table. ls _plans | wc -l returns 111.

net_new_principles.title: The system generates owner-only work faster than the owner clears it, and nothing counts the backlog
net_new_principles.principle: Any session that produces an action only the owner can take appends one row to a single _plans/OWNER_QUEUE.md: what it is, the file it came from, the consequence of not doing it, and a date. Nothing else changes and no session may invent a second place for these. SessionStart surfaces two numbers, the open count and the age of the oldest row. An owner item older than 30 days is either done, delegated to the assistant with a named workaround, or deliberately dropped with a line saying so.
net_new_principles.why: Owner-blocked items are currently scattered across at least fifteen plan files, with the two heaviest concentrations in OPS_RUNBOOK.md and BACKEND_IMPROVEMENT.md. Several are safety-critical and have been sitting since 2026-07-11: the runbook itself records pitr_enabled=false with an empty platform backup list, and asks the owner to point an uptime monitor at /api/health, both still open. The weekly self-audit surfaces its own P0 owner items into a different place again. The result is that the assistant's most valuable output, the things only a human with account access can do, is also its least trackable output. This is an owner-sustainability principle and it belongs to no technical domain, which is why twenty-six agents walked past it while individually filing the consequences (data-money-06, data-money-07, observability-1).
net_new_principles.where_it_should_live: A new _plans/OWNER_QUEUE.md, linked from _plans/ACTIVE.md and from ~/.claude/REPORT_SYSTEM.md as the destination for the Parked section's owner-only rows
net_new_principles.enforcement: SessionStart injection of the two numbers, which is a few bytes and fits the existing injection diet. The report doctrine already has a Parked section; this gives it one durable home instead of per-plan burial.
net_new_principles.local_evidence: Owner-marked lines counted per file this session: OPS_RUNBOOK.md 8, BACKEND_IMPROVEMENT.md 8, PDP_OVERHAUL.md 4, SWEEP_BACKLOG.md 3, MAP_SEARCH_REFINE.md 3, BACKEND_HEALTH_AUDIT_2026-07-14.md 3, plus nine more files with one or two each. _plans/OPS_RUNBOOK.md records 'VERIFIED 2026-07-11: pitr_enabled=false and the platform backups list is EMPTY' with an OWNER action beside it.

net_new_principles.title: One person holds every key, and there is no break-glass sheet
net_new_principles.principle: Maintain one recovery sheet, offline and outside this machine, naming every account the product depends on (Supabase, Stripe, Netlify, the domain registrar, GitHub, the email sender, Upstash), who else can reach each one, and where the recovery codes live. Update it whenever a provider is added. This is not a succession plan, it is the minimum artifact that lets anyone other than the owner stop the bleeding: put the site into a maintenance state, refund everyone, and restore the database, without this laptop and without an AI assistant.
net_new_principles.why: The estate has a detailed disaster-recovery procedure for the database and nothing at all for the loss of the person. Grepping the plans, rules and doctrine for break-glass, bus factor, continuity or succession returns nothing operational. Concretely: 1,603 commits exist only on this machine (the remote default branch is 66 days behind), the production service-role key is in one local file, and the entire recovery procedure in OPS_RUNBOOK.md is written as steps a Claude session or the owner performs. Probability is low. Consequence, once real customer money is in flight, is total, and the mitigation is one sheet of paper written once. That asymmetry is exactly the shape of thing a domain-scoped audit never proposes, because it is nobody's domain.
net_new_principles.where_it_should_live: Offline, outside the repo, with a one-line pointer in _plans/OPS_RUNBOOK.md saying it exists and where (never its contents)
net_new_principles.enforcement: None mechanical, deliberately: this artifact must not live in the repo. The only enforcement is a dated line in the runbook and a review whenever a new provider appears in the cost table.
net_new_principles.local_evidence: grep -rliE 'break.?glass|bus factor|continuity|succession' across _plans/, _rules/, _docs/ and ~/.claude/*.md returns only incidental matches (BOOKING_BACKEND_AUDIT.md, LESSONS_LEARNED.md, SOLEN_UI.md, MODEL_ROUTING.md), none of them an access-continuity artifact. Orchestrator section 11: origin/main is at 2026-05-21, local main at 2026-07-26, 1,603 commits apart.

net_new_principles.title: Every operational path is written for an agent to execute, so the owner cannot run their own product by hand
net_new_principles.principle: For each of the five operations that cannot wait, refund a booking, suspend a salon, put the site into a maintenance state, restore the database, and rotate a leaked key, the runbook carries a human-executable version: dashboard clicks, or one copy-paste command, no agent required. Each is walked once by the owner before launch and the walk is dated. If an operation has no human version, that fact is written down as a known dependency on the assistant, not left implicit.
net_new_principles.why: This is the capability half of the continuity problem and it is distinct from having the credentials. OPS_RUNBOOK.md's restore procedure is six steps ending in npm run smoke; the monitoring section describes what a cron logs; the backup path is a Next.js route triggered by a GitHub Action. All of it assumes a working toolchain and, in practice, a session. If the assistant is unavailable, changed by a provider update, or simply wrong at the moment it matters, the owner is holding a product they can only operate through an intermediary. The estate has 164 hooks teaching an assistant how to behave and not one page teaching the owner how to act alone. Writing the five is a morning's work and it also has an immediate side benefit: an operation that cannot be described as human steps is usually one that is not actually understood.
net_new_principles.where_it_should_live: A new 'by hand' section at the top of _plans/OPS_RUNBOOK.md, above the agent-oriented procedures
net_new_principles.enforcement: The walk is the enforcement: each of the five carries a 'last walked by owner' date, and a date older than six months is surfaced by the same SessionStart line as the owner queue.
net_new_principles.local_evidence: _plans/OPS_RUNBOOK.md restore procedure steps 1-6 and the in-house backup restore steps 1-6 are both written as agent or toolchain tasks (npm run smoke, npx tsx scripts/db-backup-kill-test.ts, service-role Storage API access). The monitoring section's non-agent items are explicitly marked 'not agent-doable' and remain open.

net_new_principles.title: Two floors that cannot both be satisfied need a written loser, or the session picks silently and differently every time
net_new_principles.principle: When a new floor or ceiling is added, run it against the existing floor set for the same surface. Any pair that cannot both hold at once gets one row naming which yields, under what condition, and where the tradeoff was decided. A surface that is simultaneously non-compliant in two directions is not a design problem to be re-litigated per session, it is an unarbitrated rule collision, and the fix is one row of text, not another gate.
net_new_principles.why: The estate's FLOORS LAW rule 5 already demands that every new ceiling name its floor. The symmetric obligation across domains is missing, and the collisions are already live. The imagery floor requires roughly a third of the first viewport to be photographic while the performance law sets LCP at 2.5 seconds and bans an above-fold placeholder strategy, and the two were never reconciled (hierarchy-density-09 names this and stops at the instance). The density floor demands at least four content units plus a cropped fifth on the first mobile viewport, while the type budget caps distinct sizes at four and the emphasis budget caps bold text at 30 percent, which together make a dense card grid arithmetically hard on a 390px screen. Each rule is defensible alone. Nobody owns the pair, so every session resolves it by feel, which is precisely the drift the gates were built to stop.
net_new_principles.where_it_should_live: A collisions table at the end of the FLOORS LAW block in the project CLAUDE.md, with the detail in _design-system/LOCKFILE.md
net_new_principles.enforcement: Authoring-time obligation on whoever adds a floor, plus one line in the design-verifier brief: when a screen fails two floors that the collisions table pairs, report it as an arbitration item, not as two defects.
net_new_principles.local_evidence: Project CLAUDE.md FLOORS LAW items 2, 3, 5 and 7, and NEVER-AGAIN item 2. Digest finding hierarchy-density-09 states the imagery/density-versus-LCP conflict was never reconciled; performance-02 confirms the LCP budget exists on paper and is unenforced. Orchestrator section 9 measures the live home page failing four of five floors at once with no record of which one a session should have satisfied first.

net_new_principles.title: Every check in this estate runs at authoring time; nothing ever measures the thing that is actually deployed
net_new_principles.principle: For each domain that has an authoring-time gate, add one scheduled run of the same assertion against the deployed URL, on real data, and record the result in one place. Design floors, accessibility, LCP, API response shapes and consent behaviour all already have a stated number; the run just points that number at production instead of at a file. Any law that has never been evaluated against the deployed artifact is marked as unverified-in-production in its own row until it has.
net_new_principles.why: The sweep found this in one domain and the orchestrator named it for design: floors are enforced against mockups and never against the shipped page, which is how /de home reached 4.4 percent imagery and /de/basel 0 percent while the floor was being iterated on for weeks. The generalisation is stronger than the instance. Every one of the 164 hooks fires on a Write, an Edit or a Stop. Not one observes the running product. The contract tests do not exist (api-contracts-04), the LCP budget is documented and never measured (performance-02), the accessibility rules have no scan (accessibility-09), and CI itself has never run at all because the workflow files are not on the remote default branch. So the entire enforcement estate is a very sophisticated pre-flight check for an aircraft nobody watches in the air. One scheduled production run, even weekly, changes the class of thing the estate knows.
net_new_principles.where_it_should_live: A new section in _plans/OPS_RUNBOOK.md next to monitoring, and one row per domain in ~/.claude/LAW_SYSTEM.md
net_new_principles.enforcement: One scheduled job that loads the deployed URL and runs the checks that already exist (check-geometry.mjs floors mode, an axe pass, a Lighthouse LCP number, a handful of API shape assertions) and writes a dated results file. It fails nothing at first; it just makes the deployed truth visible, which is the step that is missing.
net_new_principles.local_evidence: Orchestrator section 9 (design floors measured live: home 4.4 percent imagery and 7 distinct sizes, /de/basel 0 percent imagery and zero images of any kind on a 9,325px page) and section 11 (four workflow files exist locally, only cron-jobs.yml is on the remote, quality.yml returns HTTP 404 on the default branch, and its e2e job reports SUCCESS even when secrets are absent). Digest: performance-02, accessibility-09, api-contracts-04.

net_new_principles.title: Solen sits between two sides, holds the money, and has never declared whose side it takes
net_new_principles.principle: Write one page, customer-facing and salon-facing, stating exactly three things: what Solen decides unilaterally (refund when the salon cancels, suspension for a safety report), what it explicitly refuses to decide (subjective quality disputes), and what the recourse is when it refuses. Every dispute-touching code path maps to a line on that page, and no code path may exist that has no line. When the two sides' interests conflict and the page does not cover the case, the resolution is escalated to the owner and then added to the page.
net_new_principles.why: The shipped Terms already contain the sentence that Solen provides a reporting channel and 'is not the decision-maker in complex disputes', while the same product holds the customer's payment, owns the refund button, runs an automated strike table that can suspend either side, and moderates reviews. That is not a neutral position; it is an undeclared one, and undeclared is the worst of the three options because each individual case then gets decided by whoever is in the support inbox that day. The sweep found the mechanisms one by one (no refund reporting window, no harassment lane, no clawback policy, write-only strikes, no customer right to edit their own review) and could not see that they are all downstream of a missing stance. Deciding the stance is also what makes those five findings cheap: most of them become one sentence each once the page exists.
net_new_principles.where_it_should_live: A new public policy page linked from the Terms, with the internal version in _docs/ and each dispute code path referencing its line
net_new_principles.enforcement: Written artifact, plus the pairing rule: any new dispute, strike, refund or moderation path cites the policy line it implements in its own file header, the way lib/strikes.ts already cites ToS section 3.3 and 4.4.
net_new_principles.local_evidence: app/[locale]/terms/components/TermsContent.tsx lines 388-391: solen.ch 'provides a channel for reporting issues ... but is not the decision-maker in complex disputes', against lib/bookings/issue-refund.ts (platform-executed refunds with reverse_transfer), lib/strikes.ts (automated warning/strike/suspension writes citing ToS 3.3 and 4.4) and app/api/admin/reviews. Digest: trust-04, trust-06, trust-07, trust-08.

net_new_principles.title: A law records the fact its justification depends on, and that fact changing is its review trigger
net_new_principles.principle: Every law whose rationale rests on a condition that can change (current data volume, seed content, a one-person team, pre-launch, 28 salons) states that condition in its own row as a dependency. When the condition changes, the row is reviewed, not automatically kept and not automatically dropped. A law with no stated dependency is asserting it is unconditional, and that assertion is itself reviewable.
net_new_principles.why: The estate's existing endings machinery covers two cases: a newer decision superseding an older one (the supersession tombstone), and a gate being retired. It has no mechanism at all for a rule that quietly stops making sense because the world underneath it moved, which is the most common way law rots in a product that is about to change state completely. Live examples: the density floor's numbers were specified against seeded content, the imagery floor is currently unmeetable because salon_photos has zero rows, and every severity judgement in the estate is currently conditioned on there being no customers. On launch day dozens of rows change meaning at once and nothing marks which ones. This pairs directly with the LAUNCH.md flip list: the dependency fields are what generate that list rather than someone trying to remember.
net_new_principles.where_it_should_live: A depends-on field in the _design-system/LOCKFILE.md row format and the _design-system/TASTE_LOG.md entry template, feeding _plans/LAUNCH.md section B
net_new_principles.enforcement: Authoring-time field, plus a one-time backfill pass over the rows whose dependency is obviously pre-launch or seed-data, since those are the ones that all break on the same day.
net_new_principles.local_evidence: Project CLAUDE.md density floor ('spec + mock at IDEAL density from SEED data') and imagery floor, both written against seed content; orchestrator live check finds salon_photos with 0 rows for 28 salons and 20 of 28 covers pointing at Unsplash. ~/.claude/LAW_SYSTEM.md section 3.6 covers supersession only; digest finding gate-retirement-policy covers gate disuse only.

net_new_principles.title: The first ten of every money event are reconciled by a human, because none of these paths has ever moved real money
net_new_principles.principle: For each money-touching event class (first real booking, first payment capture, first refund, first payout to a salon, first no-show fee, first chargeback, first deletion request), the owner is notified on each of the first ten occurrences and reconciles it by hand against Stripe and the database within 24 hours, writing down what matched. Automation of that class is trusted only after those ten. If an event class reaches ten with no discrepancies, say so and stop watching it.
net_new_principles.why: Every payment, payout and refund path in this product has executed only against test data. The estate's response to that risk so far has been to add more static guarantees, which is the expensive answer, and the sweep's response is to propose more of them. The cheap answer for a one-person marketplace with no on-call rotation is to watch the first few by hand, which is what a small operator can actually do and what no domain agent proposed because none of them was thinking about the first ninety days. It is also the fastest way to discover the class of defect this estate is most prone to and cannot test for, the silent no-op: a strike table nobody reads, an SMS verification that persists nothing, a chargeback that never touches the booking. Each of those would be caught on its first real occurrence by a human comparing two screens, and by nothing else currently in the estate.
net_new_principles.where_it_should_live: _plans/LAUNCH.md section A as a launch condition, with the checklist itself in _plans/OPS_RUNBOOK.md
net_new_principles.enforcement: The founder daily digest email already exists and already reports yesterday's bookings and cron failures. Extend it with a first-ten section per event class and a counter, so the watching happens without a new system.
net_new_principles.local_evidence: _plans/OPS_RUNBOOK.md monitoring section: 'Founder daily digest email lands 05:15 UTC daily (yesterday's bookings, cron failures from cron_runs, pending reviews)'. Digest findings that are exactly this failure class: trust-01 (verification persists nothing), trust-03 (account_warnings write-only), trust-11 (chargeback never reconciled to the booking), observability-3 (automatic money paths write no audit trail).

net_new_principles.title: The assistant's autonomy must shrink on launch day, and the tier change has to be written before it is needed
net_new_principles.principle: Name, before launch, the operations the assistant may not perform unattended once real customer money exists: any write to production tables outside a reviewed migration, any use of the cron secret, any refund, payout or credit adjustment, and any run of the deletion cron. Each requires an explicit per-instance owner confirmation regardless of permission mode. This list is part of the LAUNCH.md flip list and it is written now, while it costs nothing, not on the day it starts mattering.
net_new_principles.why: Today the assistant runs in bypassPermissions with the production service-role key reachable from every worktree, and that is a reasonable trade against seed data. The trade inverts the moment a real customer's payment sits in the database, and nothing in the estate encodes the inversion. The 164 hooks are almost entirely about craft correctness, design floors, report shape and doctrine adherence; the small number that guard destructive actions guard git and the filesystem, not the database. This is the same defect as judge3-01 seen from the other end: that one says the topology is wrong, this one says the authority level is time-dependent and has no schedule. They should be fixed together, but this half costs one paragraph and can be written today.
net_new_principles.where_it_should_live: _plans/LAUNCH.md section B, and the Terminal autonomy block in the project CLAUDE.md which currently lists only git push and a few destructive commands
net_new_principles.enforcement: A single production-write-confirm gate keyed off the same LAUNCH_STATE value as judge3-03, so it is inert pre-launch and arms itself when the state flips. Building it now and testing it against a fake state is the cheap moment.
net_new_principles.local_evidence: /Users/sulo/.claude/settings.json line 4 defaultMode bypassPermissions; .env.local carries the production service-role key (judge3-01 evidence). The project CLAUDE.md Terminal autonomy block names only git push, force push, reset --hard, DB data deletion and .env.local edits as ask-first, all of them local-tooling concerns rather than production-data ones.

net_new_principles.title: A support promise is published in the Terms and was never sized against one person
net_new_principles.principle: Publish only the response time one person can keep on their worst week, state it explicitly next to the support address rather than leaving it unsaid, and measure first-response time as one of the numbers from judge3-05. Decide, before launch, the daily booking volume at which manual dispute and support handling stops working, write that number down, and write what happens when it is reached.
net_new_principles.why: The Terms publish support@solen.ch as the channel for bookings, disputes, refunds and safety reports, with no response time anywhere in the document. That is not a legal problem, it is a capacity problem wearing a legal costume: the same person writes the code, approves the salons, handles the disputes and answers the mail, and the estate has spent 410,000 words on how the product should look and none on how many messages a day that person can absorb. Unstated is also worse than slow: a customer whose stylist did not show up and who hears nothing for two days will chargeback, and a chargeback in this system does not currently update the booking at all (trust-11). Naming a number that can be kept is both the honest promise and the trigger that tells the owner when to stop taking new salons.
net_new_principles.where_it_should_live: The Terms of Service contact and dispute sections, plus a capacity line in _plans/LAUNCH.md section A
net_new_principles.enforcement: None mechanical; this is a written promise plus one measured number. The measurement rides on judge3-05's mechanism rather than needing its own.
net_new_principles.local_evidence: app/[locale]/terms/components/TermsContent.tsx line 8 and line 427 publish support@solen.ch; lines 388-391 describe the reporting channel with no deadline. grep for a response time or SLA in the terms returns nothing. Digest trust-04 independently found there is no refund reporting window either, so both ends of the support promise are open.

net_new_principles.title: Stock photography is standing in for real businesses, which is a truth problem the no-fabrication rule does not cover
net_new_principles.principle: A photograph presented as a named business's premises, staff or work must be that business's own image, with a rights attestation captured at upload. A stock or borrowed image may never occupy a slot the interface presents as belonging to a specific salon, including in seed data, including pre-launch. Where the photo is missing, render the specified non-photo fallback and file the gap as a content ticket. A design floor that cannot be met because the content does not exist is a content ticket, never a reason to borrow an image.
net_new_principles.why: The estate's no-fabrication rule is precise about numbers and status and silent about photographs, so the most legible thing on a salon card is the one element the rule does not reach. Twenty of twenty-eight salons currently carry Unsplash stock URLs as their cover, at least two salons share the same photo, and the estate's own RESTRAINT_TEST states photography must be real. Three separate problems ride on this: a customer choosing a salon by a picture of a different salon's interior, a licensing question about hotlinked stock used commercially, and a design law whose central floor is being scored against content that was never real. It is also why the imagery floor keeps failing on the live browse page while passing in mockups, since mockups pull the seeded stock and the floor was tuned against it.
net_new_principles.where_it_should_live: The no-fabrication taste rule (rule 1) in the project CLAUDE.md, extended from values to imagery, and the imagery row of the design contract
net_new_principles.enforcement: Extend the existing no-decorative-image-gate.py, which is currently on disk and unwired, to also reject a known stock-host domain (images.unsplash.com and friends) in seed data and in any salon photo field, and wire it. A duplicate-cover check over the salons table is three lines of SQL and belongs in the same pass as the duplicate-listing check (trust-10).
net_new_principles.local_evidence: Orchestrator live verification section 9: 20 of 28 salons have cover_photo_url set, every one an images.unsplash.com URL, with Belle Epil and Lisse Studio sharing photo-1570172619644; salon_photos has 0 rows; _design-system/RESTRAINT_TEST.md requires real photography, no stock. Orchestrator section 6: no-decorative-image-gate.py is cited in CLAUDE.md and REMOVED.md as a live gate and appears in neither settings file.

net_new_principles.title: The estate records what was killed and never what Solen is, so scope is defended only by precedent
net_new_principles.principle: Write one page, under 300 words, stating what Solen is and what it is not. What it is: booking and payment for Swiss beauty and wellness appointments, for customers who want a specific slot and salons who want that slot filled. What it is not, named explicitly: a salon CRM, a social network, a payments company, a messaging product, a content platform. A proposal that requires Solen to become one of those is rejected on the page, not on precedent. The page is revised only by the owner and its revisions are dated.
net_new_principles.why: The estate currently defends scope with a graveyard: gift cards, chat, last-minute, Pakete and dog grooming were each individually killed and recorded in REMOVED.md, and the exists-check protocol makes sure a killed thing is not re-proposed. That is a good mechanism for the second time an idea appears and useless for the first, which is when the decision actually costs something. It also puts the owner in the position of being the only filter, one idea at a time, forever. A positive scope statement is the cheapest instrument in this whole report: it lets a session reject a plausible feature on principle, it gives the design law something to serve other than its own consistency, and it is the missing premise behind half the estate's stranded workstreams (a dashboard CRM, a discovery feed, a loyalty system) which are each defensible alone and only questionable against a boundary that was never drawn.
net_new_principles.where_it_should_live: A new _docs/WHAT_SOLEN_IS.md, referenced from the top of the project CLAUDE.md and from the exists-check protocol as the check that runs before the graveyard check
net_new_principles.enforcement: The exists-check protocol gains one step ahead of its existing two: does this proposal fit the scope page. No new hook; the ordering is the enforcement, and the page is short enough to be read every time, unlike the 410,000 words behind it.
net_new_principles.local_evidence: _design-system/REMOVED.md and memory entry project_killed_features.md record gift cards, Pakete UI, last-minute, chat and dog-grooming as individually killed. The project CLAUDE.md exists-check protocol has three layers, all of them backward-looking (what exists, what was removed, hook enforcement). No forward-looking scope statement exists in _docs/, _design-system/ or _plans/.
